task_statement:
Research question (as posed on 2026-05-23, in the area of defensive suppression and counter strategy (best/avoid)):
If PNR fail then PULL_UP is a real league-wide counter, it should show lift>0 in >=70% of units with median lift>2pp.

Data available on that date:
- NBA 2022-23 regular season and playoffs
- NBA 2023-24 regular season and playoffs
- NBA 2024-25 regular season and playoffs
- NBA 2025-26 regular season (complete from 2026-04-13; partial before)
- NBA 2025-26 playoffs (complete from 2026-06-21; partial before)
- Sources: Per-game files from the NBA stats API: play-by-play (action type, sub-type, clock, period, score, player, shot distance and result), substitution rotation intervals, starters, defensive matchup minutes and partial possessions, box-score summary. Derived play-type possession records (initiator, play type, points) in a graph database built from the play-by-play.

Your job is to decide, before any analysis is run, whether this question can be answered with this data, what has already been established about it, which methodological and statistical risks threaten a test of it, and either a pre-registration-quality design or a reasoned recommendation not to proceed.

research_concepts: PULL_UP as a counter play type
lift in percentage points versus a baseline
unit-level consistency (share of units with lift>0, median lift)
methodological_questions: What exactly is 'lift' (PPP, eFG, or play-type share; versus which baseline) and what is a 'unit' (team-season, player, game)?
How is 'PNR fail' defined from information available before the PULL_UP possession, not from its outcome?
Is the 70% / 2pp rule adequately powered given per-unit possession counts?
How are selection, regression to the mean, shot-quality confounding and league-wide play-type efficiency baselines handled?
Does the effect hold across seasons and in the regular season versus playoffs, with a placebo counter?

historical_evidence.finding: Descriptive RS vs playoff comparison of defensive PPP allowed and possession share across 25 teams (min 30 poss per cell). Recorded: PULL_UP +0.341 PPP allowed with share -7.6pp, and PNR -0.139 with share +12.1pp. [prior work] flags LABEL_ERROR and MECHANICAL_FLOOR risks and says the PNR share jump may reflect tagging differences. No inferential test and no validation recorded.

Holdout validation of pre-game play-type PPP rankings: median rho +0.539, 88.4% of rows rho>0, median top-3 lift +0.4261 PPP, 90.8% positive lift. [prior work]'s caveat is that top-3 lift partly reflects league-wide high-efficiency play types (CUT, PUTBACK, TRANSITION). The family carries an auto-tag of C_artifact and a DRIFT_NONSTATIONARITY risk.

Within-game adaptation toward the counter play types for an inferred scheme showed an adapter advantage of about +0.05 to +0.06 PPP (p=0.0199 in one run). [prior work] is limited by selection or regression to the mean, the SWITCH subgroup reversed, and one check notes the no-signal baseline has the highest dPPP.

Matchup decomposition on 4 playoff games. Team-play-type lifts were small and mixed (e.g. PNR +1.2pp in one series, -4.1pp in another). Player-channel lifts were large but rested on n of about 15-54. Tagged A_unanswerable, with insufficient exposure and no holdout.

failed_approaches.what_failed: Inferring that shifting toward a 'counter' play type improves later PPP, using adapter versus non-adapter comparisons
failed_approaches.why: Recorded as an artifact limited by selection or regression to the mean; the effect was not consistent across scheme subgroups.

failed_approaches.what_failed: Decomposing counter lifts to defender x initiator x play-type cells on a handful of games
failed_approaches.why: Insufficient exposure (cell n of about 15-28 defensive possessions), attribution noise, and no holdout.

failed_approaches.what_failed: Treating a top-ranked play-type lift as evidence of a specific counter
failed_approaches.why: [prior work] says the lift partly reflects league-wide high-efficiency play types, so the lift is not specific to the matchup.

failed_approaches.what_failed: Reading PNR and PULL_UP shifts between RS and playoffs as defensive effects
failed_approaches.why: [prior work] flags possible tagging differences, a mechanical floor and label error, and no test was run.

evidence_establishes: No retrieved record tests the PNR-fail to PULL_UP counter hypothesis directly.
The project has recorded that PULL_UP league PPP and share shift between RS and playoffs, descriptively and on 25 teams ([prior work][prior work]).
Counter-lift claims in this project have previously been classed as artifacts of selection or regression to the mean (FAM:[prior work]).
Small-cell lift estimates in this project have been recorded as unreliable because of exposure sparsity ([prior work][prior work]).
Play-type lift measured against a naive baseline can be inflated by league-wide play-type efficiency ([prior work][prior work]).
evidence_does_not_establish: Whether PULL_UP after a failed PNR has positive lift in any specific unit, or in 70% of units.
Any causal counter effect, or the stability of the effect across seasons.
A valid outcome-independent definition of PNR failure in the derived play-type records.
own_inferences: The hypothesis as posed is underspecified: 'PNR fail', 'lift', 'unit' and the baseline are all undefined. Whether the test can pass depends on those choices.
A positive-lift share of 70% or more is easy to reach if the baseline is the average of all non-PULL_UP outcomes, because of league-wide play-type efficiency differences (a mechanical floor).
If PNR failure is defined by a poor possession result or a defender being beaten, the label is outcome-derived. Conditioning on it can create selection and regression-to-the-mean artifacts.
Team-season units have enough possessions for a share-of-units test only if PNR-fail PULL_UP counts are of the order of 100 or more per unit. That is uncertain, because this event is a narrow subset.
A pooled league-wide effect and a distribution across units are different estimands. The 70% rule is hard to separate from sampling noise without a null-calibrated benchmark.
uncertainties: How PNR failure could be identified from the play-by-play or the derived play-type records.
The number of PULL_UP possessions after a failed PNR per team-season.
Whether play-type tagging is consistent across seasons and between RS and playoffs (a tagging concern is recorded in [prior work][prior work]).
The 2025-26 playoffs are partial as of 2026-05-23, so the playoff sample is incomplete.
Only four families were retrieved, and I did not read their full records. The cut text may contain relevant details.

historical_effect.explanation: The retrieved records hold no direct answer, but they show repeated artifact patterns (selection, regression to the mean, mechanical floor, tagging error, sparse cells). That moves the decision from a plain proceed to proceed_with_changes, with a pre-specified outcome-independent label, a matched baseline, a placebo counter, and a null-calibrated threshold.
